answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and isolated to the primary region, which is the closest match to the March failover that restored latency in minutes without a write outage. A same-day release is a real competing cause, so rollback is the alternate to verify rather than execute first. Circuit breaking would fail settlement writes, which violates the no-lost-writes objective; read-replica routing does not sit on the write path; adding capacity is weaker if the fault is regional rather than headroom. Failover during peak settlement can still jeopardize in-flight writes, so downstream write-loss risk is flagged and only a guarded traffic shift is intended until the failover and rollback source records are checked.
